info.title: API Documentation
info.description:
Build reliable site-management integrations for the WordPress sites in your
account.

Use these endpoints to manage sites, review current status, and start
maintenance actions from your own tools.

## Rate Limiting

Authenticated requests are limited to 200 requests per minute per account. If the limit is exceeded, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests`.

Responses include these rate-limit headers:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: Maximum number of requests allowed per minute.
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: Number of requests remaining in the current rate-limit window.
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: Number of seconds until the current rate-limit window resets.

tags.name: Clients
tags.description:
Clients are customers or companies whose WordPress sites you manage.

Use Clients to maintain each customer's contact details and notes, and to
group the WordPress sites you manage for that customer. This makes it easier
to see who each site belongs to when reviewing clients or changing site
assignments.

tags.name: Teams
tags.description:
Team Members are people who can access your account, plus invitations you
sent that are still waiting for acceptance.

Use Team Members to see current access, pending invitations, roles, and
whether access covers all sites or only selected sites.

tags.name: Managed Accounts
tags.description:
Managed Accounts are accounts owned by other people where you have been given
access, plus invitations waiting for your decision.

Use Managed Accounts to see access granted to you: accounts you can access,
invitations waiting for your decision, your role, and whether access covers
all sites or only selected sites.

For access you grant to others, use Team Members to see who can access your
account and invitations you have sent.

tags.name: Sender Emails
tags.description:
Sender Emails are email addresses you add to your account so report and
notification emails can use them as the From address.

Use Sender Emails to see each address, whether ownership is pending or
verified, and the DKIM and return-path DNS details used to authenticate it.
DKIM details are the DNS hostname and value that help prove emails from the
address are authorized by the domain. Return-path details are the DNS
hostname and value used by the email provider to handle bounced emails and
support sender authentication.

tags.name: Tags
tags.description:
Tags are labels for grouping WordPress sites available to you.

Use Tags to review each label's name, color, and the sites assigned to it.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description:
Tasks are background actions in your account, such as WordPress updates,
staging, restores, migrations, reports, cleanup, and other site maintenance.

Use Tasks to check status and progress, review the sites and options used for
the task, and inspect site-level progress and steps when details are available.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description:
Reports are generated summaries of site activity and health for WordPress
sites available to you. Each report covers a selected date range and can
include backup activity, updates, security and firewall activity, login
activity, uptime, performance, analytics, and custom work.

Use Reports to review what happened on a site during that period, confirm
which site and client the report belongs to when available, and check the
latest email delivery status when it has been sent to recipients.

tags.name: Scheduled Reports
tags.description:
Scheduled Reports are recurring schedules that generate reports for WordPress
sites available to you.

Use Scheduled Reports to manage recurring report generation for each site,
including schedule status, frequency, next report time, report contents, and
email delivery settings.

tags.name: Report Templates
tags.description:
Report Templates define reusable report appearance, included sections,
section order, and email settings.

Use Report Templates to review and manage user-created templates, choose
templates for one-time or scheduled reports, and see where each template is
used through active or paused scheduled reports.

tags.name: Staging
tags.description:
Staging Sites are temporary WordPress sites created from backup snapshots of
live sites.

Use Staging Sites to evaluate updates, fixes, and other site changes on an
isolated copy before applying them to the live site. Each staging site also
shows its current status, expiry, PHP version, and access details.

tags.name: Auto Update Schedules
tags.description:
Auto Update Schedules are recurring schedules that run WordPress core,
plugin, and theme updates for selected sites.

Use Auto Update Schedules to manage when WordPress updates run, which sites
and update types are included, and whether backups or visual regression
checks run with the updates.

tags.name: Auto Update History
tags.description:
Auto Update History shows past runs from Auto Update Schedules for
WordPress sites in your account.

Use Auto Update History to review when scheduled WordPress updates ran,
which schedule started each run, whether an update task was created, and
which site-level core, plugin, or theme updates were included.

tags.name: Plugin Branding
tags.description:
Plugin Branding controls how your account's plugin is displayed in
WordPress admin across sites in your account.

Use Plugin Branding to review or change the plugin's displayed name,
description, author details, or whether the plugin is hidden.

tags.name: WP Login Branding
tags.description:
WP Login Branding controls the WordPress login screen shown across sites in
your account.

Use WP Login Branding to review or change the login logo, page label, error
message, help text, and sender email, and to see whether the account is
using default or custom login branding.

tags.name: Backup Destinations
tags.description:
Backup Destinations are external storage connections that can receive backup
uploads from WordPress sites in your account.

Use Backup Destinations to review available storage providers, see which
storage accounts are connected, and confirm the connection details needed
before uploading backups.

tags.name: Sites
tags.description:
Sites are WordPress sites available to you.

Use Sites as the central view of each WordPress site, including its URL,
connection and sync state, assigned client and tags, backup and security
status, server details, and WordPress update information.

tags.name: Backups Activation
tags.description:
Backups are recovery snapshots created for WordPress sites available to you.

Use Backups Activation to manage whether one WordPress site creates new
backup snapshots.

tags.name: Snapshots
tags.description:
Snapshots are saved backup recovery points for WordPress sites available to
you.

Use Snapshots to review backup history, inspect backup contents and scan
details, and choose a snapshot before starting download, upload, migration,
or restore workflows.

tags.name: Backup Download
tags.description:
Backup Downloads use completed site snapshots to package backup content for
download.

Use Backup Downloads to package all files and database tables, or only
selected paths and tables.

tags.name: Backup Upload
tags.description:
Backup Uploads use completed site snapshots to send backup content to a
connected backup destination.

Use Backup Uploads to upload all files and database tables, or only selected
paths and tables, to Dropbox or Google Drive.

tags.name: Backup Migration
tags.description:
Backup Migrations use completed site snapshots to move backup content to
another WordPress installation.

Use Backup Migrations to migrate all files and database tables, or only
selected paths and tables, to another site available to you or to an external
destination.

tags.name: Backup Restore
tags.description:
Backup Restores use completed site snapshots to restore backup content to
the same WordPress site.

Use Backup Restores to restore all files and database tables, or only
selected paths, tables, or WordPress multisite subsites.

tags.name: Files
tags.description:
Files are the backup file tree captured in completed backup snapshots for
WordPress sites available to you.

Use Files to browse backup contents, review stored file versions and totals
for files and folders, and manage which directories are included in future
backups.

tags.name: Tables
tags.description:
Tables are database tables captured in completed backup snapshots for
WordPress sites available to you.

Use Tables to browse table names, row counts, data sizes, and totals, and
manage which tables are included in future backups.

tags.name: Site Settings
tags.description:
Site Settings are site-level WordPress controls for one site in your
account.

Use Site Settings to review or change WordPress auto-updates and
WooCommerce database upgrades for that site.

tags.name: Site Plugin Branding
tags.description:
Site Plugin Branding controls how your account's plugin is displayed in
WordPress admin on one WordPress site available to you.

Use Site Plugin Branding to review or change whether that site uses default
plugin details, inherits account branding, hides the plugin, or shows a
custom displayed name, description, and author details.

tags.name: Site WP Login Branding
tags.description:
Site WP Login Branding controls how the WordPress login screen is displayed
on one WordPress site available to you.

Use Site WP Login Branding to review or change whether that site uses the
standard WordPress login screen, inherits account-level WP Login Branding,
or uses its own login logo, page label, error message, help text, and
sender email.

tags.name: Important Pages
tags.description:
Important Pages are selected page URLs on a WordPress site that need
page-specific monitoring.

Use Important Pages to keep key site pages available for page-specific
monitoring.

tags.name: WordPress Core
tags.description:
WordPress Core shows the installed WordPress version, latest available
version, update availability, and core update lock state for WordPress sites
available to you.

Use WordPress Core to review core update status and manage whether core
updates are locked for selected sites.

tags.name: WordPress Plugins
tags.description:
WordPress Plugins are installed plugin details for WordPress sites available
to you.

Use WordPress Plugins to review each site's installed plugins, versions,
update availability, activation state, package availability, security
status, and update locks.

tags.name: WordPress Themes
tags.description:
WordPress Themes are installed theme details for WordPress sites available
to you.

Use WordPress Themes to review each site's installed themes, active theme,
available updates, child-theme state, package availability, security status,
and update locks.

tags.name: WordPress Updates
tags.description:
WordPress Updates are available WordPress core, plugin, and theme updates
for sites available to you.

Use WordPress Updates to review available updates by site, compare installed
and latest versions, and apply updates with backup, sandbox, or
visual-regression options when available.

tags.name: WordPress Users
tags.description:
WordPress Users are WordPress user accounts on sites available to you.

Use WordPress Users to review user identity, role, 2FA, and default login
details across sites, and to manage user access and login settings.

tags.name: Security Activation
tags.description:
Security Activation controls whether one WordPress site available to you
uses security scanning.

Use Security Activation to turn scanning on or off and confirm whether
scanning is enabled after the change.

tags.name: Login Protection
tags.description:
Login Protection shows WordPress login attempt history for one site.

Use Login Protection to review blocked, failed, and successful login
attempts, or to view summary counts and trends for a selected time range.

tags.name: Cleanup
tags.description:
Cleanup is automatic malware cleanup for hacked WordPress sites.

Use Cleanup to confirm whether a hacked site can be cleaned automatically
and manage the connection details and post-cleanup preferences needed for
cleanup.

tags.name: Detection Summary
tags.description:
Detection Summary shows counts of potentially malicious files, scripts,
plugins, cron jobs, and redirections found by the security scanner for one
WordPress site.

Use Detection Summary to compare totals by detection type and decide where
review is needed.

tags.name: File Detections
tags.description:
File Detections are potentially malicious files found by the security
scanner for one WordPress site.

Use File Detections to review affected file paths, inspect available file
content, and decide whether detections should be treated as safe or unsafe.

tags.name: Script Detections
tags.description:
Script Detections are potentially malicious scripts found by the security
scanner for one WordPress site.

Use Script Detections to review affected scripts, threat categories,
detection locations, available script content, and mark expected scripts
safe.

tags.name: Plugin Detections
tags.description:
Plugin Detections are installed WordPress plugins classified as malicious by
the security scanner for one WordPress site.

Use Plugin Detections to review which malicious plugins were found, their
versions, activation and update state, package availability, and
vulnerability status.

tags.name: Cron Job Detections
tags.description:
Cron Job Detections are potentially malicious scheduled commands found by
the security scanner for one WordPress site.

Use Cron Job Detections to review command content and manage whether
expected commands are treated as safe.

tags.name: Redirection Detections
tags.description:
Redirection Detections are potentially malicious redirects or new-tab
destinations found on pages of one WordPress site.

Use Redirection Detections to review source pages, destination URLs,
detection times, and mark expected destination hosts safe.

tags.name: Performance Activation
tags.description:
Performance Activation controls whether one WordPress site uses performance
optimization.

Use Performance Activation to turn optimization on or off and confirm
whether optimization is enabled after the change.

tags.name: Performance Settings
tags.description:
Performance Settings are cache, JavaScript, CSS, image, and font
optimization controls for one WordPress site.

Use Performance Settings to review or change how those optimizations behave
on that site.

tags.name: Performance Reports
tags.description:
Performance Reports are the latest performance scores, metrics, and audit
details for WordPress sites available to you.

Use Performance Reports to compare site performance results or inspect the
detailed metrics and audits for one site.

tags.name: Activity Logs
tags.description:
Activity Logs are a timeline of user and site actions for one WordPress site.

Use Activity Logs to review activity across content, users, plugins, themes,
logins, and other site changes, and to manage whether new activity is
collected.

tags.name: Custom Works
tags.description:
Custom Works are manually completed work items for WordPress sites in your
account, such as maintenance, optimizations, fixes, audits, or other
reportable changes.

Use Custom Works to keep dated work history connected to each site, so
completed work can be reviewed later or included in reports.

tags.name: Notes
tags.description:
Notes are text entries attached to WordPress sites.

Use Notes to keep site context, handoff details, investigation findings,
reminders, and work history connected to each site. Previous content remains
available as note versions after edits.

tags.name: Firewall Activation
tags.description:
Firewall Activation controls whether one WordPress site uses firewall
protection.

Use Firewall Activation to turn firewall protection on or off and confirm
whether standard and advanced firewall protection are active after the
change.

tags.name: Bot Protection
tags.description:
Bot Protection controls whether one WordPress site uses bot traffic
protection.

Use Bot Protection to turn the feature on or off and review request counts
for recognized bots and blocked or unwanted bots over a selected time range.

tags.name: IP Access
tags.description:
IP Access defines trusted IPv4 or IPv6 addresses that should not be blocked
by firewall and login protection checks for one WordPress site.

Use IP Access to review, add, or remove trusted IP addresses for operators,
office networks, monitoring systems, or support workflows.

tags.name: Firewall Logs
tags.description:
Firewall Logs are request logs recorded by the firewall for one WordPress
site.

Use Firewall Logs to review recent firewall decisions, search requests, and
view request count trends for a selected time range.

tags.name: Geo Blocking
tags.description:
Geo Blocking blocks requests from selected countries for one WordPress site.

Use Geo Blocking to review blocked countries and add or remove country codes
for the site's firewall.

tags.name: WordPress Email OTP Templates
tags.description: WordPress Email OTP Templates control the plain-text message used to send sign-in codes at account level or for one site, including multisite subsite overrides.

tags.name: Code Snippets
tags.description:
Code Snippets are saved body-only PHP scripts for WordPress sites in your account.

Use Code Snippets to save reusable PHP source, list or inspect saved snippets,
remove snippets, and start background execution tasks across accessible sites.

tags.name: Security Actions
tags.description: Reset WordPress user passwords and rotate security keys for accessible sites.

tags.name: Real-Time Backups
tags.description:
Real-Time Backups capture supported site changes for one WordPress site.

Use Real-Time Backups to turn real-time backup capture on or off, and to
review the captured event timeline for that site.

tags.name: Domain Monitors
tags.description:
Domain Monitors show domain-registration monitoring state for WordPress
sites available to you.

Use Domain Monitors to list and inspect current registration monitoring
state, enable or disable monitoring for accessible sites, and request
immediate domain-registration refreshes.

tags.name: Form Monitors
tags.description:
Form Monitors watch configured form URLs for submission availability.

Use Form Monitors to list and inspect current form-monitor configuration,
create monitors for accessible sites, change monitor settings, enable or
disable selected monitors, and request immediate checks.

tags.name: Uptime Monitors
tags.description:
Uptime Monitors watch site availability for sites available to your account.

Use Uptime Monitors to list current uptime-monitor state, inspect one
monitor, enable or disable selected monitors, and inspect retained probe
observations for one accessible uptime monitor.

tags.name: SSL Monitors
tags.description:
SSL Monitors watch SSL certificate health for sites available to your
account.

Use SSL Monitors to review certificate monitoring state and inspect retained
SSL certificate probe observations, including certificate expiry,
common-name matching, chain verification, and revocation state.

tags.name: Visual Monitors
tags.description:
Visual Monitors watch selected site pages with baseline screenshots and
scheduled visual checks.

Use Visual Monitors to list, inspect, create, update, enable, disable,
delete, and refresh visual-monitor configuration across sites available to
your account.

tags.name: Page Content Monitors
tags.description:
Page Content Monitors watch configured page URLs for expected keywords.

Use Page Content Monitors to list, inspect, create, update, enable,
disable, delete, and refresh page-content monitor configuration across
sites available to your account.

tags.name: PHP Monitors
tags.description:
PHP Monitors show PHP error signatures for one WordPress site.

Use PHP Monitors to list PHP error signatures for a site and inspect one
signature's recent occurrences and stack trace.

tags.name: Vulnerability Shield
tags.description:
Vulnerability Shield helps protect a WordPress site from known
vulnerabilities by applying Virtual Patching when protection is available.

Use it to check whether Virtual Patching is active, choose the setting for
a site, or manage protection for a specific vulnerability detected on that
site.

get.description:
Returns clients in your account with contact details, notes, and assigned
site IDs. The assigned site IDs identify the WordPress sites grouped under
each client.

Use this list to review customers, find a client to update, or check which
sites are assigned to each client.

A successful response returns a paginated list of clients.

**Filtering**
- Format: `filters[field:operator]=value`
- Allowed fields: `search`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `company_name`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
- Supported operators:
  - `contains`: `search`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `company_name`
  - `gte`: `created_at`, `updated_at`
  - `lte`: `created_at`, `updated_at`
- `search:contains` searches `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, and `company_name`
- Use ISO 8601 timestamps for `created_at` and `updated_at` filters
- `timezone` applies to `created_at` filters
- Example: `filters[email:contains]=client@`

**Sorting**
- Format: `sort=field,direction`
- Sortable fields: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `company_name`
- Supported directions: `asc` (ascending), `desc` (descending)
- Default: `created_at,desc`
- Example: `sort=created_at,desc`

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order for returned clients.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Filters applied to returned clients.

post.description:
Creates a client for a customer or company and can assign existing
WordPress sites at the same time.

Use this when you need to add a customer profile and group that customer's
sites under it.

Submitted sites must be available to you and not already assigned to
another client.

A successful response returns the created client, including its assigned
site IDs.

400.description: The `client` request body is missing or contains invalid fields.

invalid_wrapper.summary: Client root key is not an object

invalid_text_type.summary: Optional text field is not a string

422.description: The client could not be created.

owner_email.summary: Cannot add account owner as client

details.message: Can't add account owner as client.

already_exists.summary: Email already exists on another client

already_assigned.summary: Site already assigned to another client

details.message: Site(a1b2c3d4e5f64789ab0c123456789def) already assigned to a client

post.description:
Removes one or more clients from your account.

Use this when a customer should no longer be tracked as a client.

Partial success is possible when some clients are removed and others are
not found.

A successful response returns removed client IDs, client IDs that could not
be removed, and delete counts.

400.description: The `ids` request field is missing, empty, or not an array.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Client ID returned in client lists and client details.

get.description:
Returns one client with contact details, notes, and assigned site IDs. The
assigned site IDs identify the WordPress sites grouped under this client.

Use this when you need to review a customer profile or check the client's
current site assignments.

A successful response returns the requested client.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Client ID returned in client lists and client details.

post.description:
Updates a client's contact details, notes, or site assignments. Site
assignments are the WordPress sites grouped under the client.

Use this when customer details change or when sites need to be added to,
removed from, or replaced in the client's assignment list.

Submitted sites must be available to you and not already assigned to
another client.

A successful response returns the updated client with its assigned site IDs.

400.description: The `client` request body contains invalid fields.

invalid_wrapper.summary: Client root key is not an object

invalid_text_type.summary: Optional text field is not a string

422.description: The client could not be updated.

owner_email.summary: Cannot add account owner as client

details.message: Can't add account owner as client.

already_exists.summary: Email already exists on another client

already_assigned.summary: Site already assigned to another client

details.message: Site(a1b2c3d4e5f64789ab0c123456789def) already assigned to a client

get.description:
Returns accounts where you already have access and invitations sent to your
email address. Each item shows the account owner email, your role, status,
and whether your access covers every site in that account.

Use this list to show accounts you can access and invitations that still
need your decision.

A successful response returns a paginated list of managed accounts.

**Filtering**
- Format: `filters[field:operator]=value`
- Allowed fields: `email`, `role`, `company_name`, `status`, `all_sites_access`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
- Supported operators:
  - `contains`: `email`, `company_name`
  - `eq`: `role`, `status`, `all_sites_access`
  - `in`: `role`, `status`
  - `gte`: `created_at`, `updated_at`
  - `lte`: `created_at`, `updated_at`
- `email:contains` matches the managed account owner's email address
- Supported role values for matching: `collaborator`, `administrator`, `co_owner`
- Supported status values for matching: `pending`, `connected`
- Boolean filters accept `true` or `false`
- Use ISO 8601 timestamps for `created_at` and `updated_at` filters
- `timezone` applies to `created_at` filters
- Example: `filters[email:contains]=owner@`

**Sorting**
- Format: `sort=field,direction`
- Sortable fields: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `status`
- Supported directions: `asc` (ascending), `desc` (descending)
- Default: `created_at,desc`
- Example: `sort=created_at,desc`

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order for returned managed accounts.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Filters applied to returned managed accounts.

parameters.name: managed_account_id
parameters.description: Managed account ID returned in managed account lists and details.

delete.description:
Leaves a managed account that you already have access to.

Use this when you no longer need access to another account.

A successful response removes your access and returns no response body.

400.description: The managed account access is not connected.

error.message: The request could not be processed due to invalid parameters.

details.message: Only connected team members can leave; use reject for pending invitations.

parameters.name: managed_account_id
parameters.description: Managed account ID returned in managed account lists and details.

post.description:
Accepts an invitation to access another person's account.

Use this when you want the invited account to appear in your managed
accounts.

The invitation must have been sent to your email address and must still be
pending. Your role and site access are chosen by the inviting account.

A successful response returns the connected managed account.

422.description: The invitation could not be accepted.

owner_email.summary: Account owner cannot be added as team member

details.message: Account owner cannot be used as team member.

parameters.name: managed_account_id
parameters.description: Managed account ID returned in managed account lists and details.

post.description:
Rejects an invitation to access another person's account.

Use this when you do not want access to the invited account.

A successful response returns the invitation with `status: rejected`.

422.description: The invitation has already been processed.

get.description:
Returns backup destinations available to your account. The list includes
storage providers that can be used for backup uploads, plus saved
destination details when a provider has been connected.

Each entry shows the provider, connection status, connected account
details when available, and upload settings.

Use this list before starting a backup upload. For Google Drive uploads,
use the saved destination `id` from the connected Google Drive entry. For
Dropbox uploads, send provider `dropbox` in the Backup Upload request.
Google Drive is omitted when that provider is disabled.

A successful response returns the available backup destinations.

Returns one backup destination by provider ID or saved destination ID.
Use provider ID `dropbox` or `google_drive` to view a storage provider,
including its current connection status. Use a saved destination `id` to
view a destination that has already been saved in your account.

Use this when you need to check one storage provider or saved destination
before using it for a backup upload.

Google Drive can be viewed only when that provider is enabled.

A successful response returns the requested backup destination.

parameters.name: backup_destination_id
parameters.description: Backup destination provider ID or saved destination ID.

post.description:
Tests one saved Dropbox or Google Drive backup destination.

Use this before starting a backup upload to check whether the saved
connection can still access the storage account. When the test succeeds,
the destination status, connected account details, and upload settings
are refreshed.

`backup_destination_id` can be a provider ID (`dropbox`, `google_drive`)
only after that provider has a saved destination in your account.

A successful response returns the tested backup destination.

parameters.name: backup_destination_id
parameters.description: Backup destination provider ID or saved destination ID.

post.description:
Disconnects one saved Dropbox or Google Drive backup destination.

Use this when the account should stop sending backup uploads to that
storage account. The saved connection and connected account details are
cleared.

`backup_destination_id` can be a provider ID (`dropbox`, `google_drive`)
only after that provider has a saved destination in your account.

A successful response returns the backup destination with
`status: inactive`.

parameters.name: backup_destination_id
parameters.description: Backup destination provider ID or saved destination ID.

get.description:
Returns sender emails in your account with display names, verification status, and DNS details.

Use this list to review configured From addresses, find a sender email ID for later requests, or check which DNS details still need verification.

A successful response returns a paginated list of sender emails.

**Filtering**
- Format: `filters[field:operator]=value`
- Allowed fields: `email`, `name`, `status`, `domain_dkim_verified`, `domain_return_path_verified`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
- Supported operators:
  - `contains`: `email`, `name`
  - `eq`: `status`, `domain_dkim_verified`, `domain_return_path_verified`
  - `gte`: `created_at`, `updated_at`
  - `lte`: `created_at`, `updated_at`
- Supported status values for matching: `pending`, `verified`
- Boolean filters accept `true` or `false`
- Use ISO 8601 timestamps for `created_at` and `updated_at` filters
- `timezone` applies to `created_at` filters
- Example: `filters[email:contains]=reports`

**Sorting**
- Format: `sort=field,direction`
- Sortable fields: `email`, `name`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
- Supported directions: `asc` (ascending), `desc` (descending)
- Default: `created_at,desc`
- Example: `sort=created_at,desc`

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order for returned sender emails.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Filters applied to returned sender emails.

post.description:
Creates a sender email for a From address and starts ownership verification.

Use this when adding an address that report or notification emails can use as the From address.

A successful response returns the created sender email with `status: pending` and its DNS details.

parameters.name: sender_email_id
parameters.description: Sender email ID returned in sender email lists and details.

get.description:
Returns one sender email from your account with verification status and DNS details.

Use this when you need the current verification status or DNS details for one address.

A successful response returns the requested sender email.

delete.description:
Deletes a sender email from your account.

Use this when an address should no longer be available for report or notification emails.

A successful response returns no response body.

parameters.name: sender_email_id
parameters.description: Sender email ID returned in sender email lists and details.

post.description:
Updates the display name or return-path hostname for a sender email.

Use this when recipients should see a different sender name, or when the return-path DNS hostname needs to change.

A successful response returns the updated sender email.

parameters.name: sender_email_id
parameters.description: Sender email ID returned in sender email lists and details.

post.description:
Requests another ownership verification email for a sender email with `status: pending`.

get.description:

visual regression options.

Use this list to review scheduled WordPress updates, find a schedule to
update, or check which sites and update types each schedule covers.

A successful response returns a paginated list of auto update schedules.

**Filtering**
- Format: `filters[field:operator]=value`
- Allowed fields: `name`, `status`, `schedule`, `update_types`,
  `site_id`, `has_backup`, `has_vr`, `started_at`, `next_update_at`,
  `created_at`, `updated_at`
- Supported operators:
  - `contains`: `name`
  - `eq`: `status`, `schedule`, `has_backup`, `has_vr`
  - `in`: `status`, `schedule`, `update_types`, `site_id`
  - `gte`: `started_at`, `next_update_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
  - `lte`: `started_at`, `next_update_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
- Supported status values for matching: `active`, `paused`
- Supported schedule values for matching: `daily`, `weekly_on_day`,
  `biweekly`, `monthly_on_date`, `monthly_on_week`, `monthly_last_day`
- Supported update type values for matching: `plugin`, `theme`, `core`
- `update_types:in` and `site_id:in` must use array syntax, for example `filters[site_id:in][]=<site_id>`
- Boolean filters accept `true` or `false`
- Use ISO 8601 timestamps for `started_at`, `next_update_at`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` filters
- `timezone` applies to `created_at` filters
- Example: `filters[status:eq]=active`

**Sorting**
- Format: `sort=field,direction`
- Sortable fields: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `name`, `status`,
  `schedule`, `started_at`, `next_update_at`
- Supported directions: `asc` (ascending), `desc` (descending)
- Default: `created_at,desc`
- Example: `sort=next_update_at,asc`

Send `paths` only when `migration.scope.include_files` is `true`, and
send `tables` only when `migration.scope.include_database` is `true`.
Internal migrations may omit `migration.connection` or use HTTP with
optional HTTP Basic Auth credentials. External migrations require
`migration.connection.method` set to `ftp`, server credentials, and
database credentials.

When real-time events are enabled,
`migration.options.real_time_events.until` is required and must be an
timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

A successful response returns the task created for the backup migration.
Use the returned task ID with Tasks to check status.

`restore.scope.subsite_ids` is accepted only for multisite sites. When
sent, subsite IDs are expanded to matching paths and tables before the
restore starts. Explicit `paths` or `tables` override generated subsite
selections for that content type.

accept only optional HTTP Basic Auth credentials. FTP restores require
server and database credentials.

`restore.options.real_time_events.until` is required and must be an
timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

snapshot.

**Filtering**
- Format: `filters[field:operator]=value`
- Allowed fields: `status`, `modified_at`, `name`, `size`
- Supported operators:
  - `eq`: `status`
  - `gte`: `modified_at`, `size`
  - `lte`: `modified_at`, `size`
  - `contains`: `name`
- Supported status values for matching: `synced`, `skipped`
- `name:contains` matches the file or folder basename and is case-sensitive
- Use ISO 8601 timestamps for `modified_at` filters
- `size` filter values must be non-negative integers
- Example: `filters[name:contains]=index`

- Format: `filters[field:operator]=value`
- Allowed fields: `name`, `rows`, `size`, `status`

  - `gte`: `rows`, `size`
  - `lte`: `rows`, `size`

- Sortable fields: `name`, `rows`, `size`
- Supported directions: `asc` (ascending), `desc` (descending)

get.description:
Returns available WordPress updates for sites available to you. Each
site can include WordPress core, plugin, and theme update details when
matching updates exist.

Use this list to review available updates, compare installed and latest
versions, find plugin or theme `filename` values for update requests, or
filter by update type.

If `site_ids` is omitted, all sites available to you are included.

**Filtering**
- Format: `filters[field:operator]=value`
- Allowed fields: `type`
- Supported operators:
  - `in`: `type`
- Allowed `type` values: `core`, `plugin`, `theme`
- `filters[type:in][]` must be sent as an array
- Example: `filters[type:in][]=plugin&filters[type:in][]=theme`
- Omit `filters` to include all update types

**Sorting**
- Format: `sort=field,direction`
- Sortable fields: `id`, `last_sync_at`
- Supported directions: `asc` (ascending), `desc` (descending)
- Default: `id,asc`
- Example: `sort=last_sync_at,desc`

A successful response returns a paginated list of available WordPress
updates by site.

should start.

get.description:

- Format: `filters[field:operator]=value`
- Allowed fields: `status`, `created_at`

  - `lte`: `created_at`
- Known `status:eq` values include `running`, `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled`

- Use ISO 8601 timestamps for `created_at` filters
- Example: `filters[status:eq]=completed`

- Format: `sort=field,direction`
- Sortable fields: `created_at`
- Supported directions: `asc` (ascending), `desc` (descending)
- Default: `created_at,desc`
- Example: `sort=created_at,desc`

Client.description:
Client details for a customer or company whose WordPress sites you manage.

A client includes contact details, notes, assigned site IDs, and timestamps.
Assigned site IDs show which WordPress sites are grouped under the client;
each site can be assigned to only one client.

last_name.description: Last name for the client contact. Empty string means not provided.

address.description: Postal or business address for the client. Empty string means not provided.

note.description: Private note visible to account users. Empty string means not provided. This field does not affect access.

site_ids.description: Site IDs currently assigned to this client.

created_at.description: Time when the client was created.

updated_at.description: Time when the client was last updated.

the account owner's email.

company_name.description: Organization name associated with the client. Omit when not provided; `null` is rejected.

note.description: Private note visible to account users. Omit when not provided; `null` is rejected.

WordPress sites to assign to this client. Each site must be available to

UpdateClientRequest.description: Client details and optional site assignment replacement for updating a client. Empty or omitted bodies leave the client unchanged.

client.description:
Partial update: only supported fields included in `client` are changed.
Omit the `client` object or send an empty object to leave the client
unchanged.

- If `first_name` is sent, it must be non-blank.
- If `email` is sent, it must be non-blank, valid, and cannot be the account owner's email or one already used by another client.
- Optional text fields must be strings when included; `null` is rejected.
- Sending `site_ids` replaces the entire list of assigned sites. Send an empty array to clear assignments. Omit `site_ids` to leave assignments unchanged.
- Each submitted site must be available to you and not already assigned to another client.

TeamMember.description:
Team member details for someone who can access your account now, or an
invitation still waiting for acceptance.

The role and site access fields show what the person can do after acceptance
or while connected. `status` tells whether access is `connected` or `pending`.

name.description: Display name shown for the team member or invitation.

email.description: Email address of the member or invitee. It is set when the invitation is created and cannot be changed.

role.description:
Permission level granted to the member or invitation. Role hierarchy is
`co_owner` > `administrator` > `collaborator`.

company_name.description: Organization name associated with the member. Blank when not provided.

status.description:
Invitation lifecycle state. `pending` means the invitation has been sent but
not accepted. `connected` means the member can access the account.

all_sites_access.description: Whether access covers every site in the account.

site_ids.description: Site IDs included in the access. When `all_sites_access` is true, this list contains all sites available to the member.

two_fa_enabled.description: Whether two-factor authentication is enabled on the member's user account. Pending invitations always return `false`.

note.description: Private note visible to account users. Blank when not provided.

created_at.description: Time when the team member or invitation was created.

updated_at.description: Time when the team member or invitation was last updated.

ListTeamMembersResponse.description: Paginated list of team members and pending invitations.

meta.description: Pagination metadata for this team member and invitation list.

team_member.description: Invitation details, role, and site access to grant after acceptance.

name.description: Display name to show for the invitation and future team member.

email.description:
Email value that receives the invitation. It must be non-blank, must
not be the account owner's email, and must not already belong to an
connected team member or pending invitation.

role.description:
Role to grant after acceptance. Hierarchy:
`co_owner` > `administrator` > `collaborator`.

company_name.description: Organization name associated with the invited person. Omit when absent; `null` is rejected.

all_sites_access.description:
Whether access covers all sites in the account. Defaults to `false`
for `collaborator` and `administrator`. For `co_owner`, omitting this
field is treated as `true`.

note.description: Private note visible to account users. Omit when absent; `null` is rejected.

site_ids.description:
Site IDs to grant limited access to. Must be sites in your account.
For `collaborator` and `administrator`, at least one site ID is required
when final `all_sites_access` is `false`. Omit or send an empty array when
`all_sites_access` is `true`. Co-owners have all-sites access and cannot
have limited site access.

Fields to change for the team member or invitation. Omitted fields remain
unchanged, and the `team_member` object must contain at least one
supported update field.

name.description: Display name to show for the team member or invitation. Must be non-blank when sent.

Not updatable. If provided and differs from the current value, returns `422`.
Omit to avoid validation errors.

New role to assign. Must be non-blank when sent. Hierarchy:
`co_owner` > `administrator` > `collaborator`. Updating to `co_owner`
without sending `all_sites_access` gives all-sites access.

company_name.description: Organization name associated with the team member or invitation. Omit to leave unchanged; send an empty string to clear it; `null` is rejected.

all_sites_access.description:
Whether access covers all sites. When changing the role to `co_owner`,
omitting this field is treated as `true`.

note.description: Private note visible to account users. Omit to leave unchanged; send an empty string to clear it; `null` is rejected.

Replaces the limited-access site list. Must be sites in your account.
Sending non-empty `site_ids` without `all_sites_access` switches a
non-co-owner to limited access. Send at least one site when final
`all_sites_access` is `false`; send an empty array only when final
`all_sites_access` is `true` or the role is `co_owner`.

ListSslMonitorsFilters.description:
Supported filters grouped by operator:
`eq`: `site_id`, `enabled`, `last_probe.status`, `last_probe.certificate.revocation_status`, `interval`.
`in`: `site_id`, `last_probe.status`, `last_probe.certificate.revocation_status`, `interval`.
`contains`: `site_url`, `last_probe.certificate.common_name`, `search`.
`gte`: `last_probe.certificate.valid_until`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `last_probe.checked_at`.
`lte`: `last_probe.certificate.valid_until`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `last_probe.checked_at`.
`null`: `last_probe.certificate.valid_until`, `last_probe.checked_at`.

Inclusion filters use repeated array parameters, such as `filters[site_id:in][]=9bf3c2e7a4d8f2c1b6e9d0a3c5f7b8e1`. The `null` operator accepts only `true`.
`search:contains` matches `site_url`.
